full_text: Imagine studying physics, having run the 400 hurdles once. Four months later: Olympic champion. This is the story of Edwin Moses. His college had no running track, so he trained at public high schools between physics classes. He won gold in Montreal in 1976, in the 400 meter hurdles. A year later he lost a race in Berlin. And then he simply stopped losing. He went unbeaten for 9 years, 9 months, and 9 days: 122 consecutive races, 107 consecutive finals, four world records, another gold in Los Angeles. Even the 1980 boycott, which took a whole Olympics from him mid-streak, couldn't put a loss on the record. Madrid, June 1987, was the next time anyone beat him. He responded by winning his next ten races in a row.
